title: I002: Add multi-arch container image build and push workflow
description:
**Size:** 📦 medium
**Category:** infrastructure
**Priority:** high
**Source:** Proposed for 'There are currently no GitHub Actions for the bui'

Create `.github/workflows/container.yml` that builds and pushes a multi-arch Docker image to `ghcr.io/plexsphere/plexd` on tag push (`v*`) and main branch push.

Workflow steps:
1. Checkout code
2. Set up Docker Buildx via `docker/setup-buildx-action`
3. Login to ghcr.io via `docker/login-action` using `GITHUB_TOKEN`
4. Extract image tags via `docker/metadata-action`:
   - On tag push `v1.2.3`: tags `1.2.3`, `1.2`, `1`, `latest`
   - On main push: tag `dev`
5. Build multi-platform image (`linux/amd64,linux/arm64`) using `docker/build-push-action` with:
   - `context: .`
   - `file: deploy/docker/Dockerfile` (existing Dockerfile, already supports TARGETOS/TARGETARCH)
   - Build args for version metadata (VERSION, COMMIT, DATE) matching Dockerfile ARG patterns
   - `push: true`
   - Platform: `linux/amd64,linux/arm64`

Workflow permissions: `packages: write`, `contents: read`.

Reference existing files (read-only): `deploy/docker/Dockerfile` (already multi-stage, multi-arch ready), `deploy/kubernetes/daemonset.yaml` (references `ghcr.io/plexsphere/plexd`).

**Rationale:** The Kubernetes DaemonSet manifest references `ghcr.io/plexsphere/plexd` but no workflow pushes images there. Deploying to Kubernetes is impossible without manually building and pushing the container image. This blocks the entire container distribution channel and Kubernetes deployment path.

**Affected Areas:**
- .github/workflows/container.yml

stories.title: Developer publishes a versioned container image by pushing a git tag
stories.want: to push a git tag matching `v*` and have GitHub Actions automatically build a multi-arch container image and push it to ghcr.io with semantic version tags
stories.so_that: Kubernetes clusters and other container runtimes can pull the versioned image without manual build steps
criteria: Pushing a tag like `v1.2.3` triggers the container workflow and pushes to `ghcr.io/plexsphere/plexd`
Tag `v1.2.3` produces image tags: `1.2.3`, `1.2`, `1`, and `latest`
The image is a multi-arch manifest covering `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`
Version metadata (VERSION, COMMIT, DATE) is embedded in the image via build args matching the Dockerfile ldflags pattern
The workflow does NOT trigger on tags not matching `v*`

stories.title: Developer publishes a dev container image by pushing to main
stories.want: pushing to main to automatically build and push a multi-arch container image tagged `dev` to ghcr.io
stories.so_that: staging/dev environments can always pull the latest main build for pre-release testing
criteria: Pushing to main triggers the container workflow
The image is tagged only with `dev` (no semver tags, no `latest`)
The image is a multi-arch manifest covering `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`
Pull requests do NOT trigger the container workflow

stories.title: Kubernetes operator deploys plexd via DaemonSet using the published image
stories.want: the container image at `ghcr.io/plexsphere/plexd:latest` to exist and contain a working plexd binary for both amd64 and arm64 nodes
stories.so_that: the Kubernetes DaemonSet in `deploy/kubernetes/daemonset.yaml` can pull and run plexd without manual intervention
criteria: Image registry and name match the DaemonSet manifest: `ghcr.io/plexsphere/plexd`
The `latest` tag points to the most recent release (not dev builds)
Multi-arch manifest allows scheduling on both amd64 and arm64 nodes without image name changes
The image contains the plexd binary at `/usr/local/bin/plexd` matching the DaemonSet entrypoint

stories.title: Workflow follows project CI conventions for supply-chain hardening
stories.want: the container workflow to follow the same conventions as ci.yml for action pinning, runner configuration, and timeout settings
stories.so_that: CI/CD workflows are consistent and supply-chain hardened across the project
criteria: All GitHub Actions are pinned by full 40-character SHA hash with version comment
actions/checkout uses the same pinned SHA as ci.yml (`34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5` / v4.3.1)
Runner is `ubuntu-latest` matching ci.yml
Job has appropriate `timeout-minutes` set to prevent runaway builds

stories.title: Workflow applies least-privilege permissions
stories.want: the container workflow to request only the minimum required GitHub token permissions
stories.so_that: a compromised workflow cannot modify code, access secrets, or affect other repositories beyond writing packages
criteria: Workflow-level permissions block is explicitly declared
`packages: write` is granted (required for pushing to ghcr.io)
`contents: read` is granted (required for checkout)
No other permission scopes are granted beyond what is strictly needed
GITHUB_TOKEN is used instead of personal access tokens

stories.title: Developer verifies version metadata is embedded in the container image
stories.want: the container image to contain the correct version, commit SHA, and build date from the triggering event
stories.so_that: deployed containers report accurate version information for debugging and inventory
criteria: VERSION build arg is passed matching the git tag (on tag push) or `dev` (on main push)
COMMIT build arg is the git SHA of the triggering commit
DATE build arg is the UTC build timestamp
Build args match the Dockerfile ARG pattern: `VERSION`, `COMMIT`, `DATE`

requirements.description: The workflow SHALL trigger on git tag pushes matching `v*` and on pushes to the main branch
requirements.rationale: Tag pushes produce versioned releases; main pushes produce dev images for testing. PRs and other branches must not trigger container builds.

scenarios.name: Version tag triggers workflow
scenarios.when: a tag matching `v*` (e.g., `v1.0.0`, `v2.3.4-rc1`) is pushed to the repository
and_then: the build-and-push job runs

scenarios.name: Non-version tag does not trigger
scenarios.when: a tag not matching `v*` (e.g., `test-tag`) is pushed
scenarios.then: the container workflow does not execute

requirements.description: The workflow SHALL build a multi-platform container image for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 using Docker Buildx
requirements.rationale: Both architectures are required for Kubernetes clusters with mixed-arch nodes. Buildx produces a single multi-arch manifest.

pulling the image on arm64 gets the arm64 variant

requirements.rationale: Semantic versioning tags allow pinning to major, minor, or patch versions. The `dev` tag provides a rolling latest-from-main image.

implementation_notes:
ARCHITECTURE: Single-job workflow using Docker Buildx for multi-platform builds. Unlike the release workflow (PXD-0035) which uses a build matrix for separate binaries, the container workflow uses Buildx's native multi-platform support to produce a single manifest list in one invocation. This is simpler and produces the correct multi-arch manifest automatically.

ACTION PINS (verified via GitHub releases pages):
- actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4.3.1 (from ci.yml)
- docker/setup-buildx-action@8d2750c68a42422c14e847fe6c8ac0403b4cbd6f # v3.12.0
- docker/login-action@c94ce9fb468520275223c153574b00df6fe4bcc9 # v3.7.0
- docker/metadata-action@c299e40c65443455700f0fdfc63efafe5b349051 # v5.10.0
- docker/build-push-action@10e90e3645eae34f1e60eeb005ba3a3d33f178e8 # v6.19.2

METADATA-ACTION TAG CONFIG:
- `type=semver,pattern={{version}}` → extracts `1.2.3` from `v1.2.3`
- `type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}` → extracts `1.2`
- `type=semver,pattern={{major}}` → extracts `1`
- `type=raw,value=dev,enable={{is_default_branch}}` → produces `dev` only on main push
- The `latest` tag is automatically added by metadata-action for non-prerelease semver tags (default behavior).

BUILD ARGS: VERSION from `github.ref_name` (tag name on tag push, `main` on branch push), COMMIT from `github.sha`, DATE generated at build time. These map directly to the Dockerfile's `ARG VERSION=dev`, `ARG COMMIT=none`, `ARG DATE=unknown`.

DOCKERFILE: `deploy/docker/Dockerfile` is already multi-arch ready — it uses `ARG TARGETOS` and `ARG TARGETARCH` which Docker Buildx sets automatically for each platform in a multi-platform build. No modifications needed.

TEST SCRIPT PATTERN: Follows `deploy/docker/test_dockerfile.sh` — define pass/fail helper functions, individual test functions using grep/awk against the YAML file, sequential execution with summary. Uses grep-based parsing rather than YAML parsing for portability (no yq dependency required).

PITFALLS: (1) metadata-action `images` must be lowercase — `ghcr.io/plexsphere/plexd` is already lowercase. (2) The `enable={{is_default_branch}}` syntax in metadata-action tags requires the workflow to have a `push.branches` trigger for the default branch. (3) Build args must use the `build-args` input (hyphenated) not `build_args` (underscored) in build-push-action. (4) The metadata step needs an `id: meta` so the build step can reference `${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}` and `${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}`.
